metadata.title: Turn Large Arithmetic into Small Arithmetic
metadata.description: Use distributive law, complement multiplication, square/cube identities, and factor cancellation to compress calculations.

content.text: The biggest speed gains in this chapter come from recognizing structure before calculating. Use 999=1000−1, 9999=10000−1, 125=1000/8, and 625=10000/16.
For algebraic identities, memorize the small set that appears repeatedly: (a±b)², a²−b², (a±b)³, a³±b³, and the pair of identities for (a+b)²±(a−b)².
When a numerator and denominator share an identity-generated factor, cancel first. In many questions, the intended answer appears before any large number is computed.
Now collapse a difference of squares.
Spot the identity hidden inside a large expression.
Perfect. The goal is now to see the identity before seeing the arithmetic.
